items.status: OPEN — filed 2026-09-30 (Order 44, tracking-44's §7.3 stop; RULED by the owner: door (a), an Order 45 follow-up)
items.title: an INJECTED closure called inside `clear` of its own context should get the CLEARED state — strict reads in its literal fail to compile, safe reads get `None` — so a callback parameter typed `context tracking` and called under `tracking.clear(..)` is the STATIC `untrack` of reactive-layers.md §7.3; today the compiler refuses the call ('an injected closure is called here, but this code can be reached without an enclosing `run`'), and a callback captures its context at creation (spec §8.4), so a `clear` around the call cannot reach it
items.discussion: tracking-44 (Order 44); repro `sweeps/order44/tracking-44/finds/clear_injected/`; B458 (`Context::clear`); reactive-layers.md §7.3; the runtime guard that ships instead (a scope lasts one run — a late callback registers nothing)
items.body: RULED door (a). Build: the coverage check reads a call inside `clear` of context C as running under C's cleared state (a strict `get` in the callee's LITERAL is refused, `get_safe` answers `None`); the base callback positions (`on_change`, `effect_on_change`, the UI event handlers — which already take `context turn_scope`) take `context tracking` and call under `clear`; pins: a `track()` in a callback literal refused at compile time; a callback with `get_safe` sees `None`. Then tracking-44's runtime epoch guard becomes belt-and-braces. Sizing M; solver (context.rs) + std, Order 45.

items.kind: bug (MISCOMPILE on JS — aliasing; native refuses)
items.title: `Shared::new(x)` ALIASES the caller's value on JS: a later `write()` through the new cell mutates `x`, and `ListCell::of(xs)` followed by `push` mutates `xs`; native refuses the same program (rustc E0382) — rule 1 (a binding copies) broken at a constructor that stores its argument
items.discussion: collections-44 (Order 44); B466 (`*view` of an aggregate does not copy — the same family); B400/B457 (copy elision); shared.vl `Shared::new`, delta.vl `ListCell::of`
items.body: Making the parameter `own` fixes JS (the move ends the source binding); native then needs a clone at a non-last use. Rec: `own value` on `Shared::new`, `ListCell::of` and every std constructor that STORES its argument; the JS emitter copies at a non-last-use `own` argument as native does. Pins: mutate through the cell, read the original, both backends. Sizing S; solver + std, Order 45 FIRST (miscompile).

items.title: `f<U, R: IntoFlow<Option<U>>>(xs, \|x\| x)` cannot infer `U` when `R` is a FLOW (the closure returns a `Source<Option<T>>`/pipe): the trait argument's `U` is not read back from the flow's element — the collection operators route around it through the impl subject
items.discussion: collections-44 (Order 44, S4); B434 (the call-site path), B480 (`switch`'s `U` through `dyn Flow`) — one family: a generic bound through a trait argument at a call
items.body: Bind `U` from the flow's trait argument at the bound (`R: IntoFlow<Option<U>>` with `R = Derive<..>` whose `Flow<Option<i32>>` fixes `U`). Sizing S; solver, Order 45 with B480.

items.title: native — an injected closure's HIDDEN PARAMETERS are ordered two ways: the closure LITERAL orders them by the contexts' DECLARATION order, the closure TYPE by the clause AS WRITTEN — a clause not in declaration order builds on JS but rustc refuses it ('expected `i32`, found `Rc<str>`'); std's body clauses are written in declaration order with a comment as the workaround
items.body: One order — the declaration order — at both sites (or the written order at both). Pin a clause written out of order, identical on both backends; drop the std comment. Sizing S; native, Order 45.

items.kind: bug (native — refusal by name; the F1 S1b gap)
items.status: OPEN — filed 2026-09-30 (Order 44, tracking-44's find 2 — the third lane this order to design around it)
items.title: native — reading or writing a FIELD through a `Shared` VIEW (`s.write().n`, `s.write().n = x`) is refused by name; A142's `OwnerCell` and S6's `TrackRuns` are written WHOLE to avoid it, and `a.write().n = a.write().n + 1` (vilan/test/shared.vl) needs a temporary (the right side's borrow would stay live across the left's)
items.discussion: tracking-44 (Order 44); repro `sweeps/order44/tracking-44/finds/shared_view_field/`; native-44's find 3 (the temporary); reactive-44's `OwnerCell`; F1 S1b
items.body: Emit a field read/write through a view as a scoped borrow (read: `{ let g = s.borrow(); g.n.clone() }`; write: `s.borrow_mut().n = x`), and hoist the right-hand side into a temporary when it reads the same cell. Pins: read, write, the read-modify-write line, both backends. Then `OwnerCell`/`TrackRuns` may go back to field writes (reactive's call). Sizing S–M; native, Order 45.

items.title: native — an operator closure whose body is `cells[id]` (a non-`Copy` element read by index) fails rustc E0507 ('cannot move out of index'): an indexed read of a non-Copy element needs a clone (or a borrow) in the emitted Rust
items.discussion: collections-44 (Order 44, S4); F46/F58's family (the emitter's copy decision at a read)
items.body: The emitter clones at an indexed read of a non-Copy element that is then used by value (rule 1: a binding copies). Pin on both backends. Sizing S; native, Order 45.

items.title: native — a struct field of type `Option<\|\| V>` in a GENERIC struct is refused by name (native-44's parity 2 covered `Option<Shared<List<closure>>>`; the bare closure-typed optional field in a generic struct is the remaining shape)
items.body: Emit the field as `Option<Rc<dyn Fn() -> V>>` with the generic's bounds carried; pin a generic struct holding one, both backends. Sizing S; native, Order 45.

items.title: `RemoteSource`, `KeyedSource`, `KeyedCell` and `ListCell` answer `None` for the new `Source::identity()`, so a TRACKED read of one re-attaches its edge on EVERY run — correct, but an attach per run, and for a mirror a lease-count bump with no frame
items.discussion: tracking-44 (Order 44, S6 @2dc418d3 — `Source::identity(): Option<i32>`, default `None`; `SignalCell`/`MemoCell` return their cell's identity); rpc.vl and delta.vl were other lanes' files
items.body: One line each: return the value cell's identity (`cell_identity`) from the four types. Pin: a tracked mirror read attaches once across runs (`attaches=1`). Sizing S; std/rpc + std/delta, Order 45.

items.title: A142 S6's `Tracker` is 5 cells per stage instance plus 1 per `effect`, allocated whether or not the body tracks anything — allocate it lazily on the first `track()` (the §4.1 lazy-owner shape), which makes an untracked body free
items.discussion: tracking-44 (Order 44, S6); M92 (a nursery per run — the same lazy-allocation family); A142 §4.1
items.body: Create the `Tracker` on the first registration; pin an untracked body allocates nothing (extend the `quiet`/`busy` shape). Sizing S; std/reactive, Order 45 with M92.
